lessons.title: Drafting messages
lessons.subtitle: Week 10: Communication and writing
lessons.body:
A message draft should fit its purpose, audience, and context. Check details and tone before sending; a generated draft should not be sent automatically.

Offline practice: Draft a fictional request for a library study space and verify its details. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A message draft should fit its purpose, audience, and context. Check details and tone before sending; a generated draft should not be sent automatically.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: Editing without distortion
lessons.subtitle: Week 10: Communication and writing
lessons.body:

lessons.title: Summarising
lessons.subtitle: Week 10: Communication and writing
lessons.body:

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

lessons.title: Translation review
lessons.subtitle: Week 10: Communication and writing
lessons.body:
Translation should preserve meaning, tone, names, and important instructions. Fluent wording alone does not prove a translation is accurate.

Offline practice: List five terms a fluent speaker should review in a translated study resource. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

lessons.title: Communication portfolio
lessons.subtitle: Week 10: Communication and writing
lessons.body:
A portfolio can show an original draft, revision, and explanation of choices. Use fictional examples and describe assistance honestly.

Offline practice: Save a before-and-after message with a short note explaining two improvements. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: A portfolio can show an original draft, revision, and explanation of choices. Use fictional examples and describe assistance honestly.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
